J Clin Epidemiol. 2010;63(5):484–90. doi: http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.jclinepi.2009.05.005 PMID: 19716268 WHO recommendations must be based on the best available evidence. All relevant evidence should be identified, synthesized and presented in a comprehensive and unbiased manner. This is challenging, yet it is essential to developing valid recommendations and high-quality guidelines. Recommendations in WHO guidelines should be based on a systematic review of the scientific literature guided by specific key questions about the intervention, exposure or approach under consideration (see Chapter 7).
